findings.title: DMARC not enforced (p=none): domain can be spoofed for BEC/wire fraud

evidence.excerpt: DMARC record: v=DMARC1; p=none; rua=mailto:dmarc@brightwaterfleet.example; policy none, pct 100.

findings.deal_impact: Spoofable domain increases BEC and wire-fraud risk for the company and counterparties; require enforcement plan in diligence and post-close roadmap.

remediation.summary: Stage DMARC to quarantine then reject, align SPF/DKIM senders, and monitor rua reports.

findings.title: SPF uses soft/neutral fail

evidence.excerpt: SPF record: v=spf1 include:_spf.mailhost.example include:sendgrid.example ~all; qualifier ~all.

findings.deal_impact: Soft-fail SPF weakens sender authentication and complements DMARC non-enforcement spoofing risk.

remediation.summary: Inventory authorized senders then change SPF to -all once aligned.

findings.title: DNSSEC not enabled

evidence.excerpt: DNSSEC DS query result: enabled false.

findings.deal_impact: Un-signed DNS is a low direct deal risk but leaves resolver spoofing exposure; easy hygiene item for insurability.

remediation.summary: Enable DNSSEC at registrar/zone signer and validate DS publication.

findings.title: Publicly logged hostnames suggest exposed admin/legacy/staging systems

evidence.excerpt: Risky hostname pattern vpn; first_seen 2023-02-11, last_seen 2026-09-30; risky_hostnames_count 4.
Risky hostname pattern jenkins|old; first_seen 2021-06-03, last_seen 2026-08-14.
Risky hostname pattern staging; first_seen 2024-01-20, last_seen 2026-10-01.
Risky hostname pattern legacy; first_seen 2019-11-05, last_seen 2026-07-22.

findings.deal_impact: VPN, legacy Jenkins, staging API, and legacy portal names suggest attack surface needing validation; could affect valuation if exposed or unsupported.

remediation.summary: Validate ownership, exposure and patching of risky hosts; remove or restrict admin/legacy/staging systems.

findings.title: Large certificate footprint relative to company size

evidence.excerpt: Certificate Transparency query reported unique_hostnames 47 with risky_hostnames_count 4.

findings.deal_impact: 47 hostnames for a 201-1000 employee company suggests inventory sprawl and possible unmanaged assets.

remediation.summary: Reconcile CT hostnames to CMDB, assign owners, and decommission unused certificates/hosts.

findings.title: Deprecated TLS versions offered

evidence.excerpt: tls_support TLSv1.0 true, TLSv1.1 true, TLSv1.2 true; tls_versions TLSv1.0, TLSv1.1, TLSv1.2.

findings.deal_impact: Deprecated TLS on www weakens transport security and may fail customer/insurer baseline checks.

remediation.summary: Disable TLSv1.0/1.1, retain TLSv1.2+ with modern ciphers, and retest all hosts.

findings.title: HSTS not set

evidence.excerpt: Headers: strict-transport-security null on brightwaterfleet.example host.
Headers: strict-transport-security null on www.brightwaterfleet.example host.

findings.deal_impact: Missing HSTS leaves downgrade/SSL-stripping exposure; low-cost hygiene remediation.

remediation.summary: Set Strict-Transport-Security with appropriate max-age after confirming HTTPS-only operation.

findings.title: Internet-facing appliance listed in CISA KEV (version not verified)

evidence.excerpt: Potential exposure: KEV match CVE-PLACEHOLDER-0001, ExampleGate SSL-VPN version 7.0.11, match_tier appliance_exposed, match_level product; KEV lists products, not affected versions; version not verified.

findings.deal_impact: Potential exposure to a known-exploited internet-facing appliance is a priority diligence item; confirm patch/version urgently as it may affect deal risk and insurability.

remediation.summary: Immediately verify ExampleGate version/patch against KEV CVE, patch or isolate VPN, and hunt for compromise.

findings.title: Publicly disclosed security incident in the last 24 months

evidence.excerpt: State AG breach notice dated 2025-08-14: unauthorized access to a customer support system; approx. 3,100 individuals notified. disclosed_within_months 14, entity_match exact.

findings.deal_impact: Recent disclosed breach raises regulatory, customer-notification, and insurance disclosure risk; require incident timeline, root cause, and remediation evidence in diligence.

remediation.summary: Obtain incident report, regulator correspondence, remediation validation, and assess notification/credit-monitoring obligations.

findings.title: SOC 2 exception in logical access controls (CC6.1)

evidence.locator: Section 4 — Trust Services Criteria, Controls, Tests, and Results, row CC6.1-01
evidence.excerpt: Exception noted. 4 of 25 sampled admin accounts were not enforced for MFA. These were service-desk accounts created via a legacy provisioning script that bypassed the conditional access policy.

findings.deal_impact: 4 of 25 sampled admin accounts bypassed MFA enforcement via a legacy provisioning script, weakening administrative access to production.

remediation.summary: Remediate CC6.1 exception: MFA is enforced for all administrative access to production systems.

findings.title: SOC 2 exception in logical access controls (CC6.2)

evidence.locator: Section 4 — Trust Services Criteria, Controls, Tests, and Results, row CC6.2-01
evidence.excerpt: Exception noted. 3 of 15 terminated users retained active access for 6, 11, and 19 business days respectively.

findings.deal_impact: 3 of 15 terminated users retained active access for 6, 11, and 19 business days, exceeding the 1-business-day revocation requirement.

remediation.summary: Remediate CC6.2 exception: Access for terminated employees is revoked within 1 business day of termination.

findings.title: SOC 2 exception in security monitoring (CC7.2)

evidence.locator: Section 4 — Trust Services Criteria, Controls, Tests, and Results, row CC7.2-01
evidence.excerpt: Exception noted. For 2 consecutive weeks (Nov 10–23, 2025), alerts were forwarded to a decommissioned distribution list and were not reviewed.

findings.deal_impact: SIEM alerts were not reviewed for 2 consecutive weeks (Nov 10–23, 2025) after being forwarded to a decommissioned distribution list.

remediation.summary: Remediate CC7.2 exception: Security alerts generated by the SIEM are reviewed and triaged daily.

findings.title: SOC 2 exception in change management (CC8.1)

evidence.locator: Section 4 — Trust Services Criteria, Controls, Tests, and Results, row CC8.1-01
evidence.excerpt: Exception noted. 2 of 40 changes lacked documented approval (emergency hotfixes).

findings.deal_impact: 2 of 40 sampled production changes (emergency hotfixes) lacked documented peer approval before deployment.

remediation.summary: Remediate CC8.1 exception: Production changes are approved by a peer before deployment.

findings.title: SOC 2 report period ended more than 90 days ago; no bridge letter provided
findings.deal_impact: Report period ended 2026-03-31, 213 days before the assessment date; controls may have changed since.

remediation.summary: Obtain a bridge letter covering through 2026-10-30.

findings.title: Critical subservice organization carved out of SOC 2 scope

evidence.locator: Section 1 — Independent Service Auditor's Report, Subservice organizations; Section 3.2 — Infrastructure
evidence.excerpt: Nimbus Cloud Services is carved out of scope: infrastructure hosting.

findings.deal_impact: Nimbus Cloud Services (infrastructure hosting) is carved out of scope and is critical to production or in-scope data.

remediation.summary: Obtain the Nimbus Cloud Services SOC report and assess carve-out risk.

claim.speaker: Dana Reyes (CTO)
claim.text: Every admin account is behind MFA. No exceptions. That's been true for years. It's enforced through our conditional access policy.

contradictions.explanation: SOC 2 CC6.1 exception: 4 of 25 sampled admin accounts were not enforced for MFA, bypassing conditional access via a legacy provisioning script.

claim.speaker: Dana Reyes (CTO)
claim.text: Offboarding is automated. HR flags the termination and access is revoked same day through our identity provider.

contradictions.explanation: SOC 2 CC6.2 exception: 3 of 15 terminated users retained active access for 6, 11, and 19 business days, not same-day revocation.

claim.speaker: Dana Reyes (CTO)
claim.text: We have a 24 7 SOC through our MSSP, every alert gets looked at, nothing sits.

contradictions.explanation: SOC 2 CC7.2 exception: for 2 weeks (Nov 10-23, 2025) alerts went to a decommissioned distribution list and were not reviewed.

claim.speaker: Dana Reyes (CTO)
claim.text: We're fully locked down there. DMARC is enforced. Nobody can spoof our domain.

contradictions.explanation: DMARC record is v=DMARC1; p=none, policy none, so DMARC is not enforced and the domain can be spoofed.

claim.speaker: Dana Reyes (CTO)
claim.text: No, nothing material. We've never had a breach.

contradictions.explanation: State AG breach notice dated 2025-08-14 reports unauthorized access to a customer support system with approx. 3,100 individuals notified.

claim.speaker: Dana Reyes (CTO)
claim.text: We decommissioned the legacy stuff a while back. Everything external goes through the main app and the VPN.

contradictions.explanation: CT presence alone doesn't prove a host is live, but legacy-portal (last_seen 2026-07-22) and jenkins-old (2026-08-14) certificates within the last 12 months show active maintenance, contradicting decommissioning a while back.

claim.speaker: Dana Reyes (CTO)
claim.text: Annual third party test. The last one came back clean. No highs.

contradictions.explanation: CC4.1-01 states 2 high-severity findings were reported in the test, contradicting a clean result with no highs, despite no control exceptions noted.

claim.speaker: Dana Reyes (CTO)
claim.text: Daily backups to immutable storage in a second region and we do a restore test every quarter.

contradictions.explanation: SOC 2 A1.2-01 control was tested with no exceptions noted, positive evidence supporting the backup and restore-test claim for that control.

claim.speaker: Dana Reyes (CTO)
claim.text: We can get one. one we haven't needed it so far.

contradictions.explanation: SOC 2 Section 5 states management plans to obtain a bridge letter covering April 1, 2026 forward upon request, corroborating that one can be obtained.

narrative.executive_summary: Brightwater Fleet Systems is rated D at 56.82 with high confidence, deal signal escalate_full_diligence, and caps CAP-CRIT, CAP-INCIDENT, and CAP-CONTRADICTION applied [F-008] [F-009] [C-001]. GV scores 29.0 and PR 35.2, versus ID 66.4, DE 82.0, RS 82.0, and RC 100.0 [F-014] [F-001]. The top exposure is a potential known-exploited internet-facing ExampleGate appliance, version not verified [F-008]. A disclosed incident dated 2025-08-14 involved unauthorized access to a customer support system, with approx. 3,100 individuals notified [F-009]. Admin-access risk is elevated because sampled admin accounts bypassed MFA via a legacy provisioning script [F-010]. Terminated-user risk is elevated because sampled terminated users retained access beyond the revocation requirement [F-011]. Detection risk is elevated because SIEM alerts went to a decommissioned list and were not reviewed [F-012]. BEC/wire-fraud risk is elevated because DMARC is p=none and not enforced [F-001]. Management credibility is materially impaired: claims of universal MFA, same-day offboarding, continuous alert review, enforced DMARC, and no breach are contradicted [C-001] [C-002] [C-003] [C-004] [C-005]. Claims that legacy systems were decommissioned and third-party testing had no highs are also contradicted [C-006] [C-007]. Next, under escalate_full_diligence, require the days_0_30 ExampleGate action before signing [F-008], complete days_31_60 incident, DMARC, access, and monitoring diligence before closing [F-009] [F-001] [F-010] [F-011] [F-012], and reflect the plan total of 142000 USD to 643000 USD in protections and covenants for days_61_100 and post_100 items [F-002] [F-013] [F-003].
key_questions_for_management: What is the verified ExampleGate version and patch status against CVE-PLACEHOLDER-0001, and what compromise-hunt evidence supports that the VPN was not exploited [F-008]?

Why did the CTO state the company had never had a breach [C-005] when the State AG notice dated 2025-08-14 reports unauthorized access and approx. 3,100 individuals notified [F-009], and where are the incident report, regulator correspondence, root cause, and remediation validation [F-009] [C-005]?

Which admin accounts bypassed MFA through the legacy provisioning script, when was the script removed, and what evidence proves MFA is now enforced for all administrative access to production [F-010] [C-001]?

Why did sampled terminated users retain access for 6, 11, and 19 business days despite the claimed same-day automated offboarding, and what control evidence now proves revocation within 1 business day [F-011] [C-002]?

What alerts, intrusions, or incidents may have been missed while SIEM alerts went to a decommissioned distribution list from Nov 10–23, 2025, and what daily triage evidence is now produced [F-012] [C-003]?

What is the sender-by-sender plan and timetable to move DMARC from p=none to quarantine and then reject, and to change SPF from ~all to -all without disrupting legitimate mail [F-001] [F-002] [C-004]?
Which of vpn, jenkins-old, staging-api, and legacy-portal are still live, externally reachable, supported, and patched, despite the claim that legacy systems were decommissioned [F-004] [C-006]?

When will management provide the bridge letter covering through 2026-10-30 and the Nimbus Cloud Services SOC report for the carved-out infrastructure hosting, and how are the reported high-severity third-party test findings being remediated [F-014] [F-015] [C-007]?
